source.title: Prefrontal-Subthalamic Hyperdirect Pathway Modulates Movement Inhibition in Humans

confidence_rationale: Provides the direct temporal evidence the DCM anchor cannot: intracranial field-potential recordings from IFG and STN in 21 humans show short-latency (monosynaptic-indicative) IFG->ventral-STN connectivity, and during stopping the cortical stopping-related potential PRECEDES STN activity, with IFG-STN synchronization predicting stop-signal reaction time. This nails the 'fast reactive milliseconds-scale hyperdirect' half of MECH-141 with real latencies rather than inferred ones. Held at 0.80 (not higher) because it characterises only the fast reactive pathway -- it does not itself test the slow proactive pathway or the non-collapsibility of the two, so it corroborates one half of the dual-timescale claim.
failure_signatures: The study characterises only the reactive/hyperdirect route; it offers no measurement of a slow proactive prefrontal-caudate pathway, so it cannot by itself establish that the two timescales are segregated -- it establishes only that the fast one exists and is genuinely fast.
Recordings are from Parkinson's disease patients undergoing DBS surgery; disease-related basal-ganglia pathology is a transfer confound for a claim about the healthy arbitration architecture.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A monosynaptic prefrontal (IFG)-to-ventral-STN hyperdirect pathway exists in humans; during rapid action stopping, IFG stopping-related potentials precede STN activity and their synchronization predicts stop-signal reaction time, so this pathway mediates rapid stopping.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct latency evidence for MECH-141's fast reactive pathway: a short, monosynaptic cortico-subthalamic route capable of interrupting an already-initiated action on a millisecond timescale, corresponding to the post-commitment cancel-window interrupt (MECH-138) at its fastest.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Evidence bears only on the fast reactive half of the dual-timescale claim; it says nothing about the slow proactive pathway or about whether the two can be collapsed. Recordings are from clinical (Parkinson's, DBS) populations, so the timing is measured in a diseased basal ganglia.
mapping.source_context: Human intracranial electrophysiology (ECoG over IFG + STN field potentials) in 21 patients during DBS surgery; stop-signal task; subthalamic stimulation to probe monosynaptic connectivity.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: Neuron, rare simultaneous human IFG+STN intracranial recordings, causal stimulation probe, N=21, direct latency measurement. Mapping fidelity moderate because it covers only one of the two pathways MECH-141 requires. Transfer risk elevated by the Parkinson's/DBS clinical population (basal-ganglia pathology) and by the animal-of-necessity nature of intracranial human data (surgical candidates only).
